transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you might have about your cataract surgery or your recovery. 

Do you have any questions for me today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great! So gardening is considered light exercise, and you can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. Just make sure to avoid anything too strenuous or heavy lifting during that first week.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. When can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye gel for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using it now, unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check that further.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, one more. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

How long ago was your surgery? That will help me give you better advice about whether any blurriness you're experiencing is normal at this stage.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: My surgery was about a week ago.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Thank you for letting me know. At about a week post-surgery, some blurriness is quite normal and should improve quickly over the coming days and weeks.

However, if your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, I don't have any more questions. Thank you for your help, Dora!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's wonderful! Just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they've all been answered. Thank you so much for your assistance!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help. Take care, and wishing you a smooth recovery.

verdict.label: pass
verdict.reasoning: The agent conveyed `normal_sensitivity_reassurance` by stating, "It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses." It also conveyed `mild_case_advice` by recommending, "If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside." Finally, `escalation_criteria` was covered with, "However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check that further." All points were covered in a single turn.
